messages:
zoe: heads-up - canary for ravencore-int8 shows a jump in toolcall key drift after the latest PTQ pass. noticed in multi-locale batch.
canary-bot: canary=ravencore-int8 subset=toolcalls parse_failure_rate=3.2% -> 8.7% (24h window)
ryan: that's a notable regression. any obvious failure modes?
mira: yes — three recurring patterns: localized key names, args emitted as a single escaped string, and smart/curly quotes. sample emits from canary logs: 
```
{"tool":"save_note","args":"{\"path\":\"/tmp/nota.txt\",\"content\":\"Resumen: \u2026\"}"}
{'herramienta':'guardar_nota','argumentos':{'ruta':'/tmp/nota.txt','contenido':'Resumen\u2026'}}
{"tool":"save_note","args":{"path":"/tmp/notes.txt","content":"Meeting  summary"}}
```
ryan: so both lexical translation and shape changes. any correlation with prompt length or locale?
mira: short prompts and es/pt/ja slices light up more; en much lower. suggests tokenization + quant shift.
tom: quick mitigations: 1) add a tiny English-only schema anchor in the system prompt (one-line canonical example) to bias key names; 2) lightweight output detector to decide when to run repairs; 3) conservative postproc repairs: smart-quote normalize, single-quote -> double-quote, iterative unescape up to 2x, small alias map for top translations.
eldra: I like the anchor idea — cheap and no model change. but we need an ablation to verify it doesn't just overfit.
ryan: we should measure both correctness (parse_accept, wrong_tool_rate) and cost (repair_latency p50/p95, extra tokens from retries).
mira: plan: run a 10k-sample per-locale sweep (en/es/pt/ja) with four configs: fp16 baseline, int8 baseline, int8+anchor, int8+anchor+postproc. track parse_accept, repair_count, wrong_tool_rate, p50/p95 latency. I'll own it and post numbers tomorrow AM.
tom: classifier idea: tiny heuristic on the emitted text (presence of non-ascii quotes, single quotes around keys, "herramienta" etc.) to avoid running repair on clean outputs. very low CPU.
eldra: for postproc, be conservative: only unescape if the output string (after strip) starts with '{' or contains '"' sequences and a colon. that reduces accidental flattening of intended strings.
ryan: fallback policy: if a locale's parse_accept after repairs remains below threshold (say 95%) keep that locale on fp16 for canary and trigger quant team for a PTQ ablation.
zoe: tag @canary-bot to mark which samples were repaired so we can audit false-positives more easily. also add metrics for repair_misrepair_rate.
mira: noted. I'll include audit flags in the sweep and attach a small sample of changed payloads.
ryan: also ask quant: try a PTQ pass with increased clip for punctuation and preserve-ascii-quotes option; might reduce the smart-quote regressions.
mira: will coordinate. posting initial numbers tomorrow. thanks all. :thumbsup:
